title: Suggest 2-of-2 Co-Resolve: Cross-Author Confirmation
desc: When wkappbot suggest resolve is called by a different channel than the suggest author, requires 2-of-2 confirmation before marking resolved. Prevents maintainer fake bulk-resolves.
steps: resolver_channel = AbbreviateCwd(CWD) compared case-insensitively to suggest.from

Cross-author 1st resolve: writes half_resolved_by/note/at/skill + half_resolved_evidence (script content inline) + half_resolved_evidence_ext to suggest entry, posts Slack thread asking author to confirm.
Cross-author second resolve (other party): completes 2/2, moves to history with both notes
Same-author or bug-auto: resolves immediately as before
--force reason: bypasses gate, posts override notice to Slack thread

--confirm flag: 2nd-party confirmation path. Skips ALL evidence file checks (goto SkipEvidenceChecks). Only requires --skill. Moves to BOTH resolver history (wkappbot.hq/) AND suggester history ({suggest.cwd}/.wkappbot/).
Verified 2026-04-26: test-suggest-resolve-coresolve.sh (resolve ts=2026-04-26T10:44:21.4731572Z)

AUTO-CONFIRM (Eye-side, runs at startup + hourly): suggest auto-confirm [--dry-run]. Pre-check binary built after half_resolved_at → run stored evidence script in this context → pass: --confirm → history. fail: stays HALF.

SUGGESTER CHECK (author-side, ID only): wkappbot suggest check <ts>. Shows: fixed-by + note + runs regression script → PASSED/FAILED. Offers 'suggest check <ts> --confirm' or add-requirement. No evidence flags needed for original author.

BUG DIAGNOSIS 2026-07-14 (Haiku sector, ts=2026-07-07T13:24:08): suggest check --confirm can permanently deadlock when a 1st-party half-resolve stored ZERO --requirement entries (evidence-script-only). SuggestCommand.cs ~line 2058-2065 unconditionally sets reqAllPass=false whenever reqs.Count==0, regardless of whether the evidence script itself passed -- so canConfirm (line 2069, regRc==0 && reqAllPass) can never become true. Worse, add-requirement is blocked post-half-resolve (frozen to protect the 2-of-2 anti-fake-resolve guarantee), so there is no workaround once in this state -- a true deadlock. Proposed fix (not yet applied): when reqs.Count==0, treat it as vacuously satisfied IF the evidence script passed (reqAllPass=true only in that case), not unconditionally false. Needs ROOT verification before implementing (Haiku diagnosis, not independently confirmed). //why:deadlock confirmed no fix available //why:deadlock has no session workaround route //why:permanently deadlock zero requirements half-resolve stored //why:permanently deadlock zero requirements half-resolve stored-sonnet //why:deadlock confirmed no fix available-haiku //why:deadlock confirmed no fix available-sonnet

DUAL HISTORY: on full resolve, appends to (1) {wkappbot.hq}/suggestions_history.jsonl (resolver/WKAppBot) AND (2) {suggest.cwd}/.wkappbot/suggestions_history.jsonl (suggester project). Each project owns its audit trail.

SUGGESTER GUARD (2026-05-01): when suggester (same channel as suggest.from) runs resolve WITHOUT --confirm: (A) if 1/2 already exists → ERROR + copy-pasteable 'suggest check <ts> --confirm', return 1. (B) if no half yet → INFO reminder that resolve is maintainer's command + 'suggest check <ts>', proceeds anyway (same-author still allowed).

suggest check --confirm flow (2026-05-07): runs regression once → if passed/skipped → calls resolve --confirm internally → history. No double regression.

Same-author self-resolve (full flow): requires --confirm --skill X --commit <hash> --class <ClassName|skill-only>. Commit message MUST contain keywords from suggest title (guard checks word-by-word). If no fix commit exists, use git commit --allow-empty -m '...' with title keywords embedded. --class skill-only for doc/skill-only changes.

CORRECT --confirm STATE-MACHINE (user spec 2026-06-05 -- the right design, vs the current bug): flow is RESOLVE -> HALF, then the suggest becomes CONFIRMABLE only after the resolve conditions are ALL-CLEAR. ALL-CLEAR means the SUGGESTER (the author) has personally EXECUTED every stored requirement and verified each actual output matches its expected pattern. COMPLETENESS IS MANDATORY: if even ONE requirement was not run, the suggest does NOT enter the confirmable state and --confirm MUST be rejected. regression + requirements PASS is a HARD PRECONDITION of --confirm, never an optional or skippable check. CURRENT BUG (filed 2026-06-05T06:28:41): the 2nd-party --confirm path does goto SkipEvidenceChecks, bypassing this state gate, so a cheap Haiku session false-confirmed a 0/3-FAIL suggest. Interim: harness WARNS (not blocks, so genuine PASS confirms still work) and the Opus suggest-QC duty (project CLAUDE.md) enforces -- NEVER --confirm unless you personally ran every requirement and all matched. Remove the warn once core fixes the state gate (no-bandaid). //why:PRECONDITION means confirm cannot bypass requirements //why:PRECONDITION means confirm cannot bypass requirements-sonnet

REQUIREMENT DESIGN RULES (learned 2026-05-09): (1) Never hardcode hwnd — session-specific, always stale next run. (2) Never test transient state (popup visible, specific dialog open) — will fail when popup gone. (3) Test behavior that is reproducible any time. (4) If bug is 'cmd X fails', requirement should test 'workaround Y works' not 'X now succeeds' — X won't succeed until fix ships.

NAVIGATION (3-tier, completed 2026-08-15): this is the PROTOCOL tier. THE DRIFT IN ONE LINE, because it changes what a session should do TODAY: step 16 here says the harness WARNS, not blocks, so genuine PASS confirms still work -- but it now BLOCKS unconditionally, so a session that ran the check and got a full PASS is refused anyway. Record the timestamp and the PASS evidence and hand it to the owner rather than routing around the guard. DESIGN PHILOSOPHY refined (user 2026-06-05): the security boundary is IDENTITY, not evidence-paranoia. (1) GENEROUS to a verified SUGGESTER: once a confirmer is proven to BE the suggest author, TRUST them -- they filed the bug, they ran their requirements, they know; give latitude on resolve/confirm, do not re-litigate evidence endlessly. (2) RAZOR-SHARP IDENTITY CHECK: the logic that verifies 'is this actually the suggester?' must be strict and unspoofable -- THAT is where rigor belongs. The 2026-06-05 false-confirm happened because identity was LOOSE: a different SESSION in the same suggest.cwd could --confirm, but cwd-match is NOT identity -- with 4 Claudes across different repos and multiple sessions per repo, cwd alone cannot distinguish the suggester session from another session in the same folder. Harden the IDENTITY gate (author/session signature), not the evidence gate. (3) WHY (the user's real concern): the cost of the bypass/backdoor cat-and-mouse is WASTED TIME + TOKENS, not moral offense. Authenticate-once-then-trust is EFFICIENT (one strict identity check, then generous) and beats an evidence arms-race that burns cache_read on every confirm. Minimizing token+time churn is the goal QC actually serves -- design for that, not for enforcement theater.

DECISION: LAUNCHER MISBEHAVING? RUN THE SAME COMMAND AGAINST wkappbot-core.exe INSTEAD OF RETRYING wkappbot. WHEN: the failure looks like the LAUNCHER rather than your command -- a HANG or TIMEOUT on submit, the eye PENDING CO-RESOLVE banner silently swallowing a submit, a '[PIPE] no LAUNCH JSON within timeout' line, mojibake in the launcher's own output, or anything that works under core but not under the wrapper. HOW: re-issue the IDENTICAL command as 'wkappbot-core.exe suggest "text" --requirement "cmd => expected" ...' -- do NOT reword the command first, because the fault is upstream of your arguments so a reworded command fails identically and costs another full timeout; and CHECK WHETHER THE FIRST ATTEMPT ACTUALLY LANDED before resubmitting, since a killed submit that registered anyway becomes a duplicate. WHY: measured 2026-08-28 in wkappbot-kih. A 'wkappbot suggest' submission exceeded 120s, was killed, was retried, exceeded 180s and was killed again; NEITHER registered, confirmed by the backlog's newest entry never changing across both attempts, with 1331 active entries. I was one keystroke from rewording the command a third time. The shape is what makes this worth a step rather than a footnote: the path for REPORTING a bug is the slowest path in the toolchain, so bugs go unfiled exactly when a session is already over budget and least able to spend three minutes on a submit. Filed as a mandatory optimisation target under wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate. CONFIRMED SAME DAY IN A SECOND REPO, and this closes the open half of the recipe: in personal-docs three launcher submissions died at the 120s timeout printing NOTHING, not even a start banner, and none of the three registered -- then the identical text through wkappbot-core.exe was accepted in seconds and returned id 1787896883.880849. So the core-direct workaround is not merely worth trying, it WORKS. TWO THINGS THE SECOND INSTANCE ADDS: reads are unaffected, suggest list returned instantly between the failed writes, so a working read is NOT evidence the command is healthy; and the owner had to point this step out to me after my third retry, because I never opened this skill -- the rule was already written and I paid the full 120s three times for not reading it. A SLOW COMMAND IS A REASON TO OPEN ITS SKILL, NOT A REASON TO RETRY IT. NOTE ALSO: core-direct is sanctioned for suggest only; a skill verb through wkappbot-core.exe is hard-blocked as a pace-accounting dodge.
